item.title: Exactness
item.description:
go-plot’s model and defaults are matplotlib’s so that a figure can be checked against matplotlib’s rendering of the same figure, not only look like it.

All fixtures are generated by scripts in tools/ from matplotlib itself (3.11.2), committed, //go:embed-ded in the tests, and compared exactly unless stated.

Ticks

what how it is checked
Tick locations, labels, offset text on linear and log axes ticker/testdata/ticks.json: 408 axes of real figures (4 sizes, 37 linear and 14 log ranges, x and y): every location bit for bit, every label and offset character for character, minor log ticks and their labels included.
Locator and formatter parameters a default figure never uses ticker/testdata/units.json: 45 MaxNLocator (nbins, steps, integer, symmetric, prune, min_n_ticks), 42 LogLocator (base 2, e, 10; subs list/auto/all; numticks), 72 ScalarFormatter (math text, no offset, fixed power limits, no scientific, ASCII minus, one or no location), 25 LogFormatterSciNotation, nonsingular, and %g. Exact, except base-e log locations, compared to 1e-15: NumPy’s e**n and Go’s math.Pow(e, n) differ in the last bit.

Colours

what how it is checked
Colormaps viridis, plasma, inferno, magma, cividis, gray, coolwarm, RdBu (and _r): the 256-entry tables are generated from matplotlib, and an independent fixture of 1008 samples per map (including the ends and out-of-range values) is compared as floats and as bytes; the test also checks that all 256 entries were sampled.
Named colours and the cycle all 148 CSS4, 10 tab:, 8 single-letter colours, C0–C9, grey levels, short and long hex: exact.

Layout

what how it is checked
Layout testdata/layout.json: 15 kinds of figure at two sizes — line, bar, barh, hist, imshow, imshow + colorbar, scatter, log-log, fill + errorbar, contourf, 2x2 grid, twinx, offsets, axhline/axvline, inverted and singular limits: every Axes position (after aspect and colorbar) and view limits (after margins and sticky edges) to 1e-9 relative, and every tick label and offset text exactly.
TightLayout matplotlib’s _auto_adjust_subplotpars, ported; testdata/layout.json holds matplotlib’s positions after fig.tight_layout() for 6 kinds of figure at two sizes (single Axes, labelled, 2x2 labelled, twinx with two labels, offsets, log-log). Every Axes edge is within 0.005 of the figure (worst measured 0.0049, 2.4 pixels): the algorithm is the same, the measured width of text is not — matplotlib’s is FreeType’s hinted box, every glyph a whole number of pixels; go-plot’s is the string’s advance.
Defaults figure 6.4 x 4.8 in at 100 dpi, subplot parameters, font sizes, tick sizes and pads, line widths, marker sizes, dash patterns (scaled by line width), patch and grid colours, legend geometry, colorbar fraction/pad/aspect: transcribed from matplotlibrc and checked by the rendering comparison below.

Algorithms

what how it is checked
Histogram binning NumPy’s algorithm (equal bins by arithmetic, corrected against the edges; explicit edges by searchsorted).
Contour levels ContourSet._autolev (MaxNLocator(n+1, min_n_ticks=1), trimmed).
Dense lines matplotlib’s PathSimplifier (threshold 1/9 pixel), ported from path_converters.h.

Rendering comparison

tools/compare draws twelve reference figures with go-plot and with matplotlib — same data, size and dpi — and measures each pair with one detector applied to both images: the axes frames (columns and rows of long dark runs), the tick marks (dark for the three pixels just outside each bottom and left spine, within the frame), and the pixels of the first cycle colour inside the frames. Tolerances: frame and ticks within 1 pixel, C0 pixel count within 10 %, overlap of C0 pixels (each side dilated by 1 pixel) at least 0.90.

figure frames ticks (go / mpl) tick error C0 pixels (go / mpl) overlap mean abs diff (0–255)
line equal 15 / 15 0 px 1695 / 1736 1.000 1.01
scatter + colorbar equal 11 / 11 0 px – – 0.53
bars (1x2) equal 26 / 26 0 px 76024 / 76034 1.000 0.67
hist equal 17 / 17 0 px 49515 / 49515 1.000 0.63
imshow + colorbar equal 16 / 16 0 px 38429 / 38683 1.000 0.77
contourf + contour + colorbar equal 16 / 16 0 px – – 0.75
log-log with grid equal 11 / 11 0 px 770 / 775 1.000 0.64
errorbar, fill, axhline/axvline, text, annotate equal 14 / 14 0 px 1688 / 1558 0.994 1.03
twinx equal 11 / 11 0 px 881 / 891 1.000 0.94
2x2 grid, offsets equal 41 / 41 0 px 4991 / 4944 0.997 1.79
int32 ndarray with markers equal 14 / 14 0 px 2380 / 2465 1.000 0.32
1000² imshow (perf figure) equal 10 / 10 0 px 17426 / 17629 1.000 1.59
2x2 labelled, TightLayout ±2 px 14 / 14 2 px 713 / 700 0.970 6.71
1e6-point line (perf figure) equal 13 / 13 0 px 12032 / 15405 1.000 2.07

In twelve of the fourteen, every frame lands on the same pixel rows and columns and every tick on the same pixel. The images were also looked at, side by side.

Two fail the tolerances, and are reported rather than loosened:

  • TightLayout: frames and ticks within 2 pixels, not 1, for the reason given above — the width of tick labels, which tight layout makes room for, is measured differently. Side by side the figures are not distinguishable by eye.
  • The dense line: go-plot paints 22 % fewer saturated C0 pixels. Every go-plot pixel is within one pixel of a matplotlib one (overlap 1.000); the difference is how dark the edges of a stroke that crosses itself thousands of times come out — Agg’s scanline accumulates such a stroke differently from go-gfx’s coverage sweep. It is not the simplification: drawn without it, go-plot’s count changes by 0.3 %, while matplotlib’s own simplified and unsimplified renderings differ by 9 %.

Negative controls

A comparison that cannot fail proves nothing. Two deliberately perturbed go-plot figures are compared with matplotlib’s line, and both must fail:

  • line_shifted, the x limits widened by 0.1 data units at the left: tick error 4 px, overlap 0.436;
  • line_1px, the view slid by 0.03 data units, 1.35 pixels: tick error 2 px, overlap 0.779.

Both are caught; the smaller one by the tick detector and by the overlap, so a one-pixel slip of the data does not pass.

Reproduce 

git clone https://github.com/go-plot/plot && cd plot
go test ./... # includes the matplotlib fixtures
uv run --with matplotlib --with numpy python tools/gen_ticks.py # regenerate a fixture
cd tools/compare && go run . -out DIR && uv run --with matplotlib --with numpy python figures.py DIR \
 && uv run --with matplotlib --with numpy python compare.py DIR line=line ...

Write rendered images to a directory outside the repository.

What does not equal matplotlib is on Differences.

item.title: Differences from matplotlib
item.description:
What is equal, and how it is checked, is on Exactness. This page is the rest.

What does not equal matplotlib

Text

Glyphs are filled outlines (go-gfx coverage), not FreeType’s hinted rasterisation with matplotlib’s text antialiasing, so the pixels of text differ, and a string’s box is its advance where matplotlib’s is FreeType’s hinted box (up to a few pixels wider on long labels). Positions are matplotlib’s (Text._get_layout: line metrics from the OS/2 table, alignment, rotation, anchoring), and like Agg the pen is put on a whole pixel. Kerning comes from DejaVu’s GPOS/kern tables through go-opentype.

Math text is TeX, not mathtext

$...$ is typeset by go-tex/math with STIX Two Math — real TeX layout (fractions, radicals, big operators, limits, matrices, \left...\right), which matplotlib’s mathtext only approximates. The exception is \mathdefault{...}, what matplotlib’s tick formatters emit: it is set in DejaVu Sans with mathtext’s own superscript rules, so tick labels match matplotlib’s look and position. See TeX labels.

Strokes

Anti-aliasing is go-gfx’s, not Agg’s; widths, caps, joins and dashes are matplotlib’s. Pixel snapping follows matplotlib’s rule (odd widths at pixel centres, even at edges) for paths made of horizontal and vertical segments. Strokes of more than 512 segments are drawn in pieces and get round ends (see performance).

Images

Images are resampled nearest-neighbour when enlarged and box-averaged when reduced; matplotlib’s default (interpolation="auto", antialiased resampling in data space) differs when an image is shown smaller than its resolution, or less than three times enlarged.

Contours

Contours are marching squares with the saddle resolved by the cell mean, not contourpy’s serial algorithm (corner_mask, chunking): levels and colours are matplotlib’s, line vertices differ slightly. Filled bands are drawn per grid cell.

Legend “best”

"best" counts the vertices, segments, boxes and scatter points under each of the nine candidate positions and takes the first with none, else the least; matplotlib’s badness also weights offsets and is computed in display space with a pad. Usually the same place; not always.

Annotate

Annotate draws arrowstyle="->" only, shrunk 2 points at both ends.

SVG

The SVG carries the same geometry but not matplotlib’s document structure, ids or metadata.

Since v0.2.0 the SVG can be inlined in an HTML page served under a strict Content-Security-Policy:

  • Paint is in presentation attributes (fill="…"), not style="…", which a style-src without 'unsafe-inline' would drop.
  • There is no script and no event attribute.
  • No reference leaves the document.
  • Text is glyph outlines, so no label can become markup.
  • A clip’s id is derived from its rectangle, so two figures inlined in one page cannot clip each other.

The one data: URI is an Imshow image.

Pie

Pie is ax.pie with matplotlib’s defaults. It differs in six places:

  • The refusals (negative, NaN, infinite, all zero) are returned as ErrPieNegative, ErrPieNonFinite and ErrPieZero, not raised.
  • A sum of sizes that overflows is taken after scaling, where matplotlib draws every wedge empty.
  • AutoPct takes Go format verbs ("%1.1f%%" works in both; Python’s %d is Go’s %.0f).
  • labeldistance=None is LabelDistance(math.NaN()).
  • There is no shadow, no hatch and no frame=True.
  • Donut, PlainText (labels never reach TeX) and SpreadLabels (labels of thin wedges moved apart, with leader lines) are go-plot’s own.

No module-level pyplot

plt.plot, plt.xlabel and the other functions acting on a hidden current Axes are not provided, by design: see the API.

Not in v0

  • suptitle, and TightLayout with explicit pads or rect;
  • symlog, logit and date axes;
  • minor ticks on linear axes (off by default in matplotlib too) and AutoMinorLocator;
  • constrained_layout;
  • subplots sharing;
  • hatching;
  • boxplot, violin, quiver, stem, step, pcolormesh, 3-D;
  • colorbar extend and discrete norms;
  • image interpolation other than nearest;
  • Text bounding boxes;
  • legend columns, titles and bbox_to_anchor;
  • native and browser windows (go-widgets/window);
  • PDF output.
